claims.statement: GitHub pull-request review ingress is POST /webhooks/github: it verifies the X-Hub-Signature-256 signature, records deliveries, rejects unsupported events/actions, routes only workspace-owned repositories, returns 503 on an unreadable workspace lookup, and schedules accepted review work as FastAPI background tasks.

Automatic first review accepts opened and ready_for_review PR actions only for repositories explicitly opted into auto-review; the enabled-repository store defaults absent repositories to disabled and fails soft on store errors. Draft review is additionally controlled by the PR author's effective review_draft_prs preference.

The request_pr_review tool parses a GitHub PR URL and preserves an active Slack thread; trigger_pr_review_from_ref fetches authoritative PR metadata, rejects drafts or missing prerequisites, creates the canonical reviewer thread, stores PR/head/watch metadata, posts an in-progress comment, and dispatches the reviewer assistant.
Reviewer and scout thread IDs are deterministic UUIDv5 values derived from the owner, repository, PR number, and role; these formulas are cross-process persisted-data routing contracts.

Reviewer preparation uses a replaceable per-thread sandbox and GitHub App token, checks out the PR, materializes either the initial or re-review diff, and computes changed lines for local anchor validation; it concurrently loads PR, existing-thread, guidance, and base-commit policy context.

Reviewer prompt construction treats PR descriptions and review-thread bodies as untrusted data by XML delimiting them and neutralizing closing tags, while the reviewer graph exposes review-specific tools rather than authoring tools.

For eligible reviews, the reviewer awaits a head-specific review-scout walkthrough: the scout reuses an active run for the same head or launches a durable run, persists ordered diff steps, and the reviewer continues without it when it times out or fails.

Findings are stored against a pull request in PostgreSQL while reviewer-thread metadata retains PR routing state; legacy metadata findings are copied on first access, and database mutations lock the PR finding state, operate on fresh records, and merge replacement snapshots by ID.

add_finding validates generated titles, severity/confidence/side enums, line-range order, and changed-diff anchors; it rejects out-of-diff anchors without retry, permits non-inline file-level findings, deduplicates open findings by fingerprint, and drops suggestions longer than four lines while retaining the finding.
A missing reviewer thread is surfaced to reviewer tools as a structured thread_not_found result with an explicit do-not-retry instruction.

publish_review requires a complete unique ranking of expected candidates, publishes only open in-diff unpublished findings at or above the severity threshold, and on re-review limits new publication to findings first seen at the live head SHA.

Publication resolves the current head SHA from thread metadata, emits one GitHub PR Review with marker-bearing inline comments, and records review and marker-matched comment identities together so later reconciliation and resolve-on-fix can safely target the surfaced finding.

Publication deliberately handles nonstandard outcomes: evaluation is a dry run; an empty re-review with an existing Open SWE review skips another summary while advancing review state; unresolved-anchor 422 responses prune identifiable invalid anchors and retry once; and invalid GitHub authentication invalidates the cached token.

Watch-mode push handling only re-reviews a watched canonical reviewer thread with a changed PR diff; unchanged diffs advance last_reviewed_sha and create a settled success check on the new head, while changed diffs reconcile threads, update the live head, create a new check, and dispatch re_review.

Reconciliation identifies a finding's GitHub thread primarily through the embedded marker, backfills publication identity, records the latest human reply after the bot comment as reassessment-required, and marks a finding resolved only when all matched threads are resolved; outdated threads alone do not resolve it.

A non-bot reply to an Open SWE review comment reconciles state, records a human_reply interaction associated with the parent finding, and dispatches a reviewer run with reviewer_event='finding_reply'.

Automatic first and changed-diff reviews track an Open SWE Review check in reviewer metadata; completion clears its ID only after a successful GitHub PATCH and preserves a pending result on failure, while after-agent middleware settles an unfinished run as neutral or retries that pending real result.
Reviewer-focused tests cover auto-review gates, watch and unchanged-diff behavior, findings and tools, reconciliation, publishing outcomes, and scout checkout/diff-step ownership.
